body:
OBSERVED in source 2026-08-23. Deliberately NOT claimed as runtime-verified — see the caveat below,
which is the whole reason this is filed the way it is.

The native reader pins itself to the viewport and scrolls an inner div:
`frontend/src/pages/NativeReader.module.css:1` — `.shell { position: fixed; inset: 0; … }`
`frontend/src/pages/NativeReader.module.css:10` — `.body { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow: auto; }`

So the document does not scroll; that `<div>` does. It carries no `tabIndex` and no accessible name
(`frontend/src/pages/NativeReader.tsx`), and the TXT content inside it is a plain `<pre>` with no
interactive descendants — `.text` sets `white-space: pre-wrap` with no overflow of its own, so there
is nothing else for the keyboard to land on.

A scrollable `<div>` with no `tabindex` and no focusable children is reachable by keyboard only in
engines that implement keyboard-focusable scrollers. Firefox does. Chrome added it (127+). **Safari
does not** — which is every browser on iPadOS, the platform this reader was specifically fixed for
in #1584. There a keyboard user cannot scroll a long text file at all.

Classic does not have this hole: it binds arrow keys explicitly
(`cps/static/js/reading/txt_reader.js:27-41`), so its TXT reader is keyboard-operable everywhere.

WHY THIS IS NOT RUNTIME-VERIFIED, stated plainly rather than papered over: the harness drives
Chromium, and Chromium is the engine that DOES focus scrollers — so a passing Playwright check
would confirm nothing about the browser where this actually bites. The discriminating test needs
WebKit. Until someone runs it there, treat the Safari half as reasoned from documented engine
behaviour, not measured.

That uncertainty does not block the fix, which is correct in every engine either way: give the
scroll container `tabIndex={0}` and an accessible name (`role="region"` + `aria-label`), so it is
focusable and announced regardless of engine heuristics. Compare F-062863 — same reader, the
separate question of whether continuous scroll should replace classic's paging.
title: The native reader's scroll container is not keyboard-reachable, so TXT is unscrollable by keyboard on Safari
